messages:
maria: Heads up: ap-south1 nvme read-retry spike since 04:12 UTC, ~18% of gnode-pool failing attach. GPU provisioning queue jumped.
alex: Can you paste a grafana link or a quick snapshot?
maria: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panel=nvme_read_retries&node=ap-south1 — CPU looks fine but local IOPS p50/p99 latency is high. I see cleaner churn in the janitor logs.
jin: Is this the same janitor/ephemeral-cleaner thrash we saw last month? which janitor version are we running?
maria: janitor v2.3.1. Relevant log lines: `janitor[2145]: scrub: evict loop retry=5 err=EIO` — multiple partial block flags showing up.
samir: If the scrub is thrashing, we should pause janitor on the affected cohort. Can we `kubectl annotate` the controller to skip that cohort? @nora any objections?
nora: Agree. Pausing cleaner for that cohort reduced attach latency in the prior incident. I'll apply the skip annotation now.
nora: Done: `kubectl annotate scrub-controller cohort=ap-south1 cleanup.pause=true` — cluster acknowledged.
deploy-bot: Rollout started scrub-controller v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2 (patch) :rocket:
alex: Any chance this is firmware-related? vendor release notes mentioned elevated read-retries in 6.x FW on some models.
jin: We rolled FW on a subset two days ago. Quick cross-check shows host-tag gnode-apse1-batch-17 has fw 6.1, others still on 5.9. Correlation looks weak across affected nodes.
maria: Pausing cleaner already dropped pending-attach from ~420 -> ~90 in ~90s. NVMe error counters still trending up slowly though.
samir: Can you run `nvme smart-log` on an affected host and paste the output snippet?
maria: Pasted snippet: ```smart-log: critical_warning: 0, media_errors: 12, error_log_entries: 67, temperature: 46C``` — errors concentrated on write-stream bins according to our mapping.
nora: As an intermediate mitigation, throttle janitor concurrency for ap-south1. Lower it to 2 threads to reduce IO fanout.
samir: Policy applied: `janitor.concurrency=2` for nodes with label region=ap-south1.
alex: Also recommend temporary scheduler change: add soft-fallback to avoid placing new GPU launches in that cohort. Route to ap-southeast1 as fallback.
nora: Implemented soft-fallback; new GPU requests are now routed to ap-southeast1.
maria: Provisioning recovered and the queue drained. Ops follow-up: open ticket with vendor for elevated media_errors and schedule a firmware cohort test. I'll create the infra ticket with logs.
jin: Action item: run scrub dry-run on canary nodes with `--rate=low` and collect write-pattern histograms + nvme telemetry.
nora: :thumbsup: I'll coordinate a post-mortem and a cost note — routing to fallback bumped cross-region egress by ~2TB/hr while active, will estimate cost impact.
maria: Thanks everyone. Leaving thread open until vendor confirms root cause and firmware test results are in.
